## Error Model — Completeness & Clarity

- [x] CHK001 Is the failure-mode → error-code mapping specified per symbol (NULL → `NULL_HANDLE`; bad path/host/XML/enum → `CAPI_CONFIG_INVALID`; destroyed/expired/type-mismatched → `INVALID_HANDLE`; `index >= count` → `INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE`)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003/004/005/005b/007] — PASS: Per-symbol: FR-003 (`fixpp_dict_load_from_xml` → NULL_HANDLE / CAPI_CONFIG_INVALID); FR-004 (`set_tcp_endpoint` → NULL_HANDLE / CAPI_CONFIG_INVALID); FR-005 (`acceptor_bound_endpoint` → NULL_HANDLE / INVALID_HANDLE); FR-005b (`set_reset_seqnum_policy` → NULL_HANDLE / CAPI_CONFIG_INVALID); FR-007 (`field_count`/`field_at` → NULL_HANDLE / INVALID_HANDLE / INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE). All documented; no symbol left unmapped.
- [x] CHK002 Is the `*out_dict = NULL` (and `*out = NULL` generally) postcondition on EVERY failure path stated as a requirement, not just the happy path? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003] — PASS: FR-003 states "MUST set `*out_dict = NULL` on every failure path"; contracts/dictionary-loader.md: "`*out_dict` is NULL on every failure path". Stated as a MUST, covering all failure paths.
- [x] CHK003 Is "a non-empty `fixpp_strerror` string accompanies `CAPI_CONFIG_INVALID`, never an abort" specified as a measurable requirement? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004/§Edge Cases] — PASS: US1 AC2 states "a non-empty `fixpp_strerror` string — never a thrown C++ exception, never a crash"; SC-004 states "returns `FIXPP_ERR_CAPI_CONFIG_INVALID` (with a non-empty `fixpp_strerror`, no abort)"; Edge Cases: "never abort". All three sites confirm the requirement is measurable (check: `fixpp_strerror` returns a non-null, non-empty string; process continues).
- [x] CHK004 Is the construction-vs-steady thunk split specified per symbol — only `fixpp_dict_load_from_xml` translates; the steady-state symbols (`set_tcp_endpoint`, `acceptor_bound_endpoint`, `field_count`, `field_at`, `set_reset_seqnum_policy`) abort on an escaping exception? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011/§Edge Cases] — PASS: FR-011 enumerates the split: "Construction-time thunk (`fixpp_dict_load_from_xml`) MUST translate caught C++ errors to `FIXPP_ERR_CAPI_CONFIG_INVALID`; steady-state thunks (the endpoint setter, the bound-endpoint readback, the iteration accessors) MUST treat an escaping exception as an invariant violation → fatal log + `std::abort`". Edge Cases closes: "Exception escaping a steady-state thunk … → fatal log + `std::abort`, not translated (`[2i §5.2]`)".
- [x] CHK005 Is "no C++ exception may cross `extern "C"`" stated for every new symbol (not only the loader)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001/007/011] — PASS: FR-001 states "never letting an exception cross `extern "C"`" for the loader; FR-007 states "No C++ exception may cross the boundary" for field iteration; FR-011 covers all 7 symbols globally via the construction-vs-steady split (construction → translate; steady → abort). The `[2i §5.2]` reference in FR-011 and Edge Cases ties every symbol to the cross-cutting no-exception contract.

## Ownership & Lifetime — Completeness & Clarity

- [x] CHK006 Is the owning `fixpp_dict_t` model (refcounted `shared_ptr<const Dictionary>`; the dict outlives the handle while any session still references it) specified? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002/§Key Entities] — PASS: FR-002 states "releasing the consumer's `shared_ptr` reference ... The dictionary's storage persists while any session still references it (refcounted; `[2i]` line 1344)"; Key Entities: "`fixpp_dict_t` — opaque, owning (refcounted `shared_ptr<const fixpp::dict::Dictionary>`) handle"; data-model.md E-1 and contracts/dictionary-loader.md both confirm. Verified against `[2i]` line 1344: "`fixpp_dict` holds `std::shared_ptr<const fixpp::dict::Dictionary>`. `fixpp_dict_destroy` releases the shared_ptr; the dictionary lives until all sessions using it are destroyed."
- [x] CHK007 Is the tombstone double-destroy-safe requirement (a `tag_` liveness token, rewrite to `FIXPP_HANDLE_TAG_DEAD`, retain a bounded dead shell) specified AND explicitly distinguished from the single-destroy-only `fixpp_msg_destroy` discipline? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002] — PASS: FR-002 explicitly states both halves — "idempotent double-destroy-safe via a handle tombstone" (the requirement) AND "NOT the single-destroy-only `fixpp_msg_destroy` discipline" (the distinction). contracts/dictionary-loader.md states "NOT the single-destroy-only fixpp_msg_destroy discipline."
- [x] CHK008 Is the bounded dead-shell retention rationale (dicts are O(few) per process, so engine-style retention is bounded) documented so the retention choice is justified, not arbitrary? [Traceability, Spec §FR-002/§Edge Cases] — PASS: FR-002 states "retains a bounded dead shell (dicts are O(few) per process — a binding loads a handful — so engine-style retention is bounded)"; Edge Cases confirms the same rationale. The bound is justified by usage pattern (startup-time load, not per-message), matching the `fixpp_engine_destroy` precedent.
- [x] CHK009 Is the field-view validity window defined precisely — the parent handle's OWN lifetime (the dispatch window for an inbound message; until `fixpp_msg_destroy` for a 051 view-backed clone)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006/§Edge Cases] — PASS: FR-006 states "`field_out->value` MUST alias the wire buffer … valid for the parent handle's own lifetime (the dispatch window for an inbound message; until `fixpp_msg_destroy` for a 051 view-backed clone)"; data-model.md E-3 states "valid for the parent `fixpp_msg_t` handle's own lifetime — the receive-callback dispatch window for an inbound message, or until `fixpp_msg_destroy` for a 051 view-backed clone"; contracts/field-iteration.md echoes both cases.
- [x] CHK010 Is the use-after-invalidation of a `field.value` pointer documented as a consumer obligation explicitly NOT enforced on the hot path (same flyweight contract as the typed getters, `[2i §4.6]`)? [Completeness, Spec §Edge Cases] — PASS: FR-006 closes with "(Using it after that window is a documented use-after-invalidation (`[2i §4.6]`), not enforced on the hot path)"; Edge Cases: "`field_at` value pointer used after the parent handle's lifetime → a documented use-after-invalidation the consumer must avoid (same flyweight lifetime contract as the typed getters, `[2i §4.6]`); the window is the handle's own lifetime … not enforced on the hot path."

## Value Semantics & Iteration Contract

- [x] CHK011 Is the value-aliasing requirement (`field.value` aliases the wire buffer, no caller-buffer copy, ZERO global-heap) specified with a measurable guard (counting-resource + mallocnesia dual gate)? [Measurability, Spec §FR-006/SC-003] — PASS: FR-006 states "`field_out->value` MUST alias the wire buffer … no caller-buffer copy, zero global-heap"; SC-003 specifies "The iteration path is verified zero global-heap under the allocation guard (counting-resource + mallocnesia LD_PRELOAD dual gate); each `field.value` is confirmed to alias the wire buffer." Both the requirement and its measurable verification gate are stated. Confirmed realizable: `OffsetTable::entries()` returns `std::span<entry const>` (offset_table.hpp:85), each entry has `{offset, length, tag}`, so `value = wire_base + e.offset` is a zero-copy alias.
- [x] CHK012 Is the enumeration model specified OPERATIONALLY (every `OffsetTable` entry in wire/document order, one per occurrence — a multiset) rather than as a bi-directional "== typed-getter set" claim? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006/§Clarifications] — PASS: FR-006 states "enumerating every `OffsetTable` entry of the parsed message in wire/document order — one entry per wire occurrence (a tag repeated across N repeating-group instances yields N enumerated entries) … This is an operational definition (the offset table = a multiset), NOT a bi-directional … claim." The Clarifications session also records "defined operationally as every `OffsetTable` entry in wire/document order."
- [x] CHK013 Is the one-directional consistency invariant stated precisely — getter-readable tags ⊆ enumeration, matching value bytes for the FIRST occurrence, the reverse NOT holding under repeated tags? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007/SC-002] — PASS: FR-007 states "any tag a scalar typed getter (`fixpp_msg_get_string`) can read appears in the enumeration with matching value bytes for its first occurrence (getter-readable tags ⊆ enumeration). The reverse does NOT hold — under repeated tags the enumeration is a strict superset of the scalar-getter-readable set." SC-002 also names the FIRST occurrence explicitly.
- [x] CHK014 Is the no-host-out-param decision for `acceptor_bound_endpoint` (only `uint16_t` port, to avoid a host-string lifetime contract; host is consumer-known) documented as a deliberate contract choice? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005/§Key Entities] — PASS: FR-005 states "The host is the consumer-known bind host (no host-string out-param — avoids a host-string lifetime contract; the C++ surface exposes only `.port`)"; Key Entities: "(no host-string out-param — avoids a host-string lifetime contract)"; contracts/transport-endpoint.md: "The bind host is consumer-known (no host out-param — avoids a host-string lifetime contract)". Deliberate and documented.

- [x] CHK018 Is the initiator-dialing-port-0 case specified as a config error surfaced at open/start (not set-time), distinct from the acceptor port-0 OS-assign semantics? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases] — PASS: Edge Cases: "`set_tcp_endpoint` with port 0 on an initiator → an initiator dialing port 0 is a config error surfaced at open/start, not at set-time (set-time validates host non-empty + stores; the engine rejects an undialable endpoint) — documented; the port-0 OS-assign semantics apply to acceptor bind only." The two port-0 meanings are explicitly distinguished.
